subject: naming n_divergent, generality, and input checking

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: naming n_divergent, generality, and input checking
parts:
[moving to stan-dev, new subject; Jonah, I didn't know
if you were on stan-dev, so I'm cc-ing you.]

How could a trajectory recover from diverging? I'd think
we'd just add a boolean value for HMC and NUTS, neither of
which can recover from a divergent iteration (values or
gradients preventing movement due to arithmetic issues).

If we imagine some other kind of sampler where it can recover,
we can have another diagnostic. We don't need to share at
this low level. (I know Michael and I have different opinions
about this --- the biggest issue here is the command structure,
which also tries to generalize to the least common denominator
of whatever currently exists, but will then need to be modified
for new sampler types, new I/O types, different PRNG configs.)

It's in general a bad idea to try to build software to accommodate
coding errors. There's just no end to where you need to check
when you go down that road. The right thing to do is to write
unit tests to check and fix code when it breaks.

This is like the general practice for testing function inputs.
You need to test user inputs, because those the code can't control.
But you don't test inputs to internal functions, because if those go
wrong, it's a bug. For example, if I have this user facing function
that requires a positive input:

int foo(int x) {
if (x <= 0) { ... raise error ... }
bar(x);
}

Now if bar() is not a user facing function, then we don't want to
do this:

int bar(int x) {
if (x <= 0) { ... raise error ... }
...

because (a) we know bar() will only get called with positive values,
and (b) if we throw an error from an internal function back to the
user, it's confusing. The checks should ideally happen in the top-level
user-facing function.

- Bob

> On Feb 14, 2015, at 9:34 AM, Michael Betancourt <betan...@gmail.com> wrote:
>
> n_divergent is the number of divergent iterations during a
> Hamiltonian trajectory. When NUTS is implemented corrected
> it rejects dynamically at the first divergent iteration so when
> using NUTS (the Stan default) n_divergent should be 0 or 1.
> But that is not guaranteed (we may not be using NUTS and
> NUTS may not be implemented correctly).
>
> On Feb 13, 2015, at 9:49 PM, Jonah <jga...@gmail.com> wrote:
>
>> I should have read your issue comment first. I see you also find the name confusing.
>>
>> On Friday, February 13, 2015 at 4:47:30 PM UTC-5, Jonah wrote:
>> Just out of curiosity, why is it called n_divergent if it can only be 0 or 1? I would think that n_divergent would be the total number of divergent iterations, rather than an indicator. But maybe the n stands for something else here?
>>
>> On Friday, February 13, 2015 at 5:13:52 AM UTC-5, Bob Carpenter wrote:
>> I'll add a discussion in the next version of the manual.
>>
>> We could shorten the dictum to just:
>>
>> *** We can't guarantee the accuracy of your estimates. ***
>>
>> That's not just Stan, it's the basic nature of floating point.
>> Iterative, probabilistic algorithms just make things harder.
>>
>> So you'd need the same warning for basic arithmetic in every
>> language (C++, Java, R, etc.). Then you'd need to bold face it
>> and put it on every page of something like the glm() doc for R.
>>
>> What we'd like to do is be a bit more specific. I'll add a discussion
>> to the Stan language manual. Here's the issue comment:
>>
>> https://github.com/stan-dev/stan/issues/1202#issuecomment-74016969
>>
>> Right now, n_divergent is only documented in the CmdStan manual.
>> We're working on moving more and more functionality into the core
>> C++ code.
>>
>> - Bob
>>
>> > On Feb 11, 2015, at 8:23 PM, Marty <marty....@gmail.com> wrote:
>> >
>> >
>> >
>> > On Monday, September 8, 2014 at 8:28:49 AM UTC-4, Michael Betancourt wrote:
>> >
>> > Unless all of your chains report n_divergent=0 we cannot guarantee the accuracy of your Monte Carlo estimates.
>> >
>> >
>> > Just curious, but should this warning be printed in huge letters on every page of the Stan manual? Ok, I'm exaggerating, but since the inner workings of Stan are not as well known to Stan users as they are to Stan developers, this seems like a concern.

messages.author: a5e83218c834e013
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] naming n_divergent, generality, and input checking
parts:
Symplectic integrators cannot recover, so that’s not the
relevant problem. Imagine that you’re running HMC with
a static integration time and you see a bunch of divergences.
The ratio n_divergent / n_leapfrog tells you how quickly you
diverge which can be very informative and useful in practice.
n_divergent capping at 1 is _very_ specific to NUTS.

Really what should happen is that if NUTS is the current
sampler then n_divergent is not shown along with the
other parameters in any display like bin/print, but rather a
global summary is given before the parameters are printed out.
But then we’d need to have sampler-specific bin/print
behavior which is a whole ‘nother problem.

messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] naming n_divergent, generality, and input checking
parts:
> On Feb 14, 2015, at 9:32 PM, Michael Betancourt <betan...@gmail.com> wrote:
>
> Symplectic integrators cannot recover, so that’s not the
> relevant problem. Imagine that you’re running HMC with
> a static integration time and you see a bunch of divergences.
> The ratio n_divergent / n_leapfrog tells you how quickly you
> diverge which can be very informative and useful in practice.
> n_divergent capping at 1 is _very_ specific to NUTS.

This isn't worth beating to death, but I can't resist, because
it goes back to the general design issue of whether we design
for an anticipated future when we don't even have an example, or
do we just build for what we have. It's a tough judgment call
every time.

My own preference would be to tie config and output more tightly
to the samplers with less generalization.

> Really what should happen is that if NUTS is the current
> sampler then n_divergent is not shown along with the
> other parameters in any display like bin/print, but rather a
> global summary is given before the parameters are printed out.
> But then we’d need to have sampler-specific bin/print
> behavior which is a whole ‘nother problem.

Also, I was watching someone (Daniel or Rob, presumably) plot the
divergent iterations above the diagonal and non-divergent below
the diagonal in one of Ben's pairs plots from RStan. That's also
helpful to see if the divergences occur in a specific region.
I thought it would be even more helpful to plot the penultimate
state before the divergence, but that's impossible with the output
we currently provide.

- Bob

messages.subject: Re: naming n_divergent, generality, and input checking
parts:
[cc-ing stan-dev]

I sent you an invite to the dev list. If you accept,
let me know and I can give you posting priveleges.

I'm in Australia until May 1, but we need to talk about
what to do with ShinyStan (you are that Jonah, right?).
I'll be at the Stan meetings. My own feeling is that we
should separate the posterior analysis part of Stan from
the inference engine, ideally making them two R packages.
ShinyStan can be the latter. In that way, it'd be a competitor
to Coda, and provide a good place to put things like
Ben's diagnostics. I'm not sure my feeling's universal.

- Bob
